statement: Consider the graph G2 whose vertices are the pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n and grid2[i][j] = 1, and whose edges join (i,j) and (i',j') exactly when |i - i'| + |j - j'| = 1. An island of grid2 is the set of vertices of one connected component of G2. An island C of grid2 is a sub-island if for every (i,j) in C, grid1[i][j] = 1. The function returns a result r and r is exactly the number of sub-islands of grid2.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid1) and n = len(grid1[0]). Assume 1 <= m <= 500, 1 <= n <= 500, len(grid2) = m, and for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid1[i]) = n and len(grid2[i]) = n. Also assume that for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid1[i][j] ∈ {0,1} and grid2[i][j] ∈ {0,1}.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid1) and n = len(grid1[0]). Assume 1 <= m <= 500, 1 <= n <= 500, len(grid2) = m, and for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid1[i]) = n and len(grid2[i]) = n. Also assume that for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid1[i][j] ∈ {0,1} and grid2[i][j] ∈ {0,1}.

statement: Let I2 be the number of islands of grid2, where an island is a maximal 4-connected set of cells (i,j) with grid2[i][j] = 1. The function returns a result r and r <= I2.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid1) and n = len(grid1[0]). Assume 1 <= m <= 500, 1 <= n <= 500, len(grid2) = m, and for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid1[i]) = n and len(grid2[i]) = n. Also assume that for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid1[i][j] ∈ {0,1} and grid2[i][j] ∈ {0,1}.

statement: Let grid1' be any matrix of the same shape m x n with entries in {0,1} such that grid1'[i][j] = grid1[i][j] whenever grid2[i][j] = 1. Then the function returns a result r for (grid1, grid2) and the same result r for (grid1', grid2); in other words, count_sub_islands(grid1, grid2) = count_sub_islands(grid1', grid2).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid1) and n = len(grid1[0]). Assume 1 <= m <= 500, 1 <= n <= 500, len(grid2) = m, and for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid1[i]) = n and len(grid2[i]) = n. Also assume that for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid1[i][j] ∈ {0,1} and grid2[i][j] ∈ {0,1}.

statement: Let grid1' be any matrix of the same shape m x n with entries in {0,1} such that grid1'[i][j] >= grid1[i][j] for every i,j. Let r = count_sub_islands(grid1, grid2) and r' = count_sub_islands(grid1', grid2). Then both calls return results and r' >= r.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid1) and n = len(grid1[0]). Assume 1 <= m <= 500, 1 <= n <= 500, len(grid2) = m, and for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid1[i]) = n and len(grid2[i]) = n. Also assume that for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid1[i][j] ∈ {0,1} and grid2[i][j] ∈ {0,1}.

statement: Let grid1^T and grid2^T be the transposes of grid1 and grid2, so grid1^T[j][i] = grid1[i][j] and grid2^T[j][i] = grid2[i][j] for all i,j. Then the function returns a result r for (grid1, grid2) and also returns r for (grid1^T, grid2^T).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid1) and n = len(grid1[0]). Assume 1 <= m <= 500, 1 <= n <= 500, len(grid2) = m, and for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid1[i]) = n and len(grid2[i]) = n. Also assume that for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid1[i][j] ∈ {0,1} and grid2[i][j] ∈ {0,1}.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0 if and only if every island of grid2 contains at least one cell (i,j) with grid1[i][j] = 0. If grid2 has no islands, this condition is vacuously true.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid1) and n = len(grid1[0]). Assume 1 <= m <= 500, 1 <= n <= 500, len(grid2) = m, and for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid1[i]) = n and len(grid2[i]) = n. Also assume that for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid1[i][j] ∈ {0,1} and grid2[i][j] ∈ {0,1}.
